Topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: From Arrows to Spaces

Target audience: University students (Introductory Level)

Section: section_1 — What is a Vector? (Visualizing Magnitude & Direction)

Lecture lines:
Vectors are arrows with magnitude and direction.
Visualize them starting from the origin.
A bird flies from nest at origin.
To a tree at point (3,2).
This arrow represents our vector (3,2).

Planned animations:
# Animation 1 (Hook): Dot appears at origin, then grows into a vector arrow toward (3,2). Color: #FFD700 (Gold) for arrow. Label "(0,0)" at start, "(3,2)" at head.
# Animation 2 (Prerequisites): Draw grid lines lightly in #404040. Highlight (3,2) coordinate.
# Animation 3 (Definition): Label the vector as 'v'. Show the distance formula as sqrt(3^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(13). Color: #00BFFF (Deep Sky Blue) for formula.
# Animation 4 (Demonstration): Move the vector tail to (1,1) and point to (4,3). Show that the arrow shape is identical.
# Animation 5 (Application): Animate the vector as a 'path' of a bird from (0,0) to (3,2). Label path 'Bird Path'. Color: #32CD32 (Lime Green).

Section: section_2 — Vector Addition: The Parallelogram Rule

Lecture lines:
Adding vectors combines their movements.
Place the second tail at the first head.
Form a parallelogram with these two vectors.
The diagonal is the sum of vectors.
Like a boat moving across a current.

Planned animations:
# Animation 1: Show Vector A (blue) and Vector B (red). Place them starting at origin. Color A: #00BFFF, Color B: #FF4500.
# Animation 2: Shift Vector B so its tail starts at the head of A. Highlight the parallelogram formed by A and B. Color: #FFFFFF (White) for dotted outline.
# Animation 3: Draw the resultant vector (sum) from origin to the far vertex of the parallelogram. Label as 'A + B'. Color: #FFD700 (Gold).

Section: section_3 — Scalar Multiplication: Stretching the Arrow

Lecture lines:
Scaling stretches or shrinks a vector.
Multiplying by 3 triples the arrow length.
Negative scalars reverse the vector direction.

Planned animations:
# Animation 1: Show Vector V. Color: #00BFFF. Stretch V to 3V (longer arrow) and 0.5V (shorter arrow). Label each clearly.
# Animation 2: Show V then animate it rotating 180 degrees to show -V. Color: #FF4500 (Red). Highlight the reversal.
# Animation 3: Display a number line (scalar) next to the vector. As the scalar slider moves from -2 to 2, the vector scales and flips in real-time.

Section: section_4 — Linear Combinations and Basis Vectors

Lecture lines:
Basis vectors 'i' and 'j' define the space.
Any 2D vector is a combination of them.
This grid movement is a linear combination.

Planned animations:
# Animation 1: Show unit vectors i=(1,0) in #FFD700 and j=(0,1) in #32CD32. Grid background on.
# Animation 2: Represent a vector v=(3,2) as 3*i + 2*j. Show it visually as three 'i' arrows and two 'j' arrows stacking up.
# Animation 3: Fade out the grid lines. Show that any point (x,y) can be reached by a combination of i and j. Label 'Span'. Color: #FFFFFF.

Section: section_5 — Conclusion: The Power of Linear Transformations

Lecture lines:
Transformations move, rotate, and resize spaces.
These operations form the basis of AI.
Like pinching to zoom on your screen.

Planned animations:
# Animation 1: Show a 2D grid of dots. Animate the grid shifting and rotating. Label 'Transformation'. Color: #00BFFF.
# Animation 2: Simulate a 'pinch-to-zoom' on the grid. Vectors on the grid grow/shrink relative to the center. Color: #FFD700.
# Animation 3: Reveal a 2x2 matrix display changing as the grid changes. Highlight connection between matrix and vector movement. Color: #32CD32.

Section: section_1 — What is a Vector? (Visualizing Magnitude & Direction)

Lecture lines:

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        # Calculate center of the area

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are arrows with magnitude and direction.",
            "Visualize them starting from the origin.",
            "A bird flies from nest at origin.",
            "To a tree at point (3,2).",
            "This arrow represents our vector (3,2)."

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
